page.layout: Two coin medallions (engravings) at the top, side by side; below them one column of running text at full width; no marginal notes; no footnotes.

main_text.l: PHOCAS in eius Imperatoris,& Domini fui,locu succe-
dit, quę nuper imperio & vita priuarat:nec tamen ipse ab aua-
ricię vicio tęperauit,cūm caufam ei auaricia Mauricij prębuif-
fet coniurandi in caput illius:quin longę ftudiofius corradędæ
pecuniæ incubuit:& omnia ex Perficæ feruitutis inftituto egit.
Hic Romanum Pontifice[?] primarium omnium declarauit fol-
licitatus à Bonifacio 3. Cætera adeò focors & ignauus, & fre-
quentibus adulteriis infamis,ut cūm Ro.imperium undiq; bar-
bari vaftarent,ftarętque folùm eius nominis umbra, confpira-
tum fit in illum ab Heracliona,Heraclio & Prifco,qui captum
inertiffimum hominem prius interfecere quàm ferte ei fuppe-
tias eius milites potuerint,omnémq; ftirpem impuriffimi prin-
cipis fuftulēre. cœpit imperare anno mundi 4567. à Christo
nato 605. imperátque annis 8.Egna.lib.2.
HERACLIVS, qui in Phocam coniurarat, à militibus
primùm Imperator pronunciatur: populus dein & Senatus in-
genti acclamatione probant:accepto itaq; diademate à Sergio
Constantinopolitano patriarcha,Perficum bellum parat,lega-
tis antea miffis pro induciis impetrandis. Ludibrio habitus à
Perfis,adeò excanduit ut differre non potuerit: refpondebant
enim impij hoftes non prius fe Romanis pacem daturos,quàm
Christum abnegaffet Imperator.Perfide igitur omni, in ultio-
nem,igni ferróque vaftata, lignũ falutiferæ crucis recepit..Ce-
lebris adhuc eft nobis dies feftus,argumentũ victoriæ infignis:
Tigris factus eft inter utrosque limes:nouo tandem morbi ge-
nere obiit Heraclius,anno imperij 30.Pom.Læ.Egna.li.2. Tunc
Mahomethes infanus emerfit.

page.notes: Coin legends in the two medallion engravings, which are not running text: left, "IMP PHOCAS CAES AVG"; right, "IMP HERACLIVS P F AVG". Doubtful: the tilde over the e in "Pontifice" (line 5 of the first paragraph) is hard to see on the scan. Some letters in the Greek-looking heading lines and the stroke over the final vowels are faint; the transcription follows the most likely reading.
